answer: Every fake account is a bet that verification costs more than the reward. Proof of unique Dribbble shot history flips the bet — shots posted and liked across four years — and the prism lands on the attacker instead. What makes this stick is that shots posted and liked across four years cannot be faked in bulk — each proof is independent, and the horizon of independence is that one compromised proof endangers no other account. A farm could afford one proof, maybe ten, but the wharf of a hundred is measured in weeks of work and thousands in fees, against a reward that shrinks per head.
